unsupported: GhostAmbushHallway trigger activation and its command table/dispatch timing are not reconstructed.
Autonomous AI, target selection, movement/combat decisions, and AI event production are not reconstructed.
Caller producers for respawn eligibility, group membership/update, saved Limbus transforms, and complete revive/body ownership remain external.
PreSpawn focus and arbitrary transitions into Spawn outside the bounded fresh-ghost path are not reconstructed.
General enable-condition/serialized visibility and full VisualObject synchronization remain external; selected fresh Ghost visibility is now source-bound.
Timed alpha fading is not implemented or claimed; VisualObject::StartFadeIn and UpdateFadeIn are return stubs.
This kernel does not decode the original binary tables; its Catalog must preserve CharacterTable row order and the original template slots.
The original random draw and its per-actor seed/call-order effects are not reproduced. No default variant is selected.
The kernel does not resolve the 224 default/type/base/gear/saved property fields, evaluate ClassID formulas, instantiate Character objects, or integrate into the renderer/actor factory.
MGP editor template inheritance/asset placement semantics beyond the observed exact runtime key are not reconstructed.
No per-actor original slot is claimed without the timer seed and every preceding ordinary-stream draw/construction-order dependency.
The adapter does not own, seed, reset, or globalize the random streams; caller supplies and retains their state.
Cached property-ID early return, player/savegame selection, actor construction, template-to-CharacterTable mapping, and property/class resolution are separate paths or modules.
Negative slot counts are rejected as malformed adapter input; only the observed empty and positive template-count branches are supported.
This is not the independent port/game-data CombatRandom stream and does not alter combat RNG semantics.
This adapter does not resolve generated level/module placement; callers provide the final GameObject world position and scale.
Zone::IsInside and its PhysicalObject guard remain a separate predicate. The trigger's AABB activation path must not acquire that guard.
No scene node, _colzone node, selector, Irrlicht collision callback, or renderer state is inferred or required by this contact path.
Online activation, multi-player policy, move-out scripts, all-player scripts, one-player effects, and associated-door bindings are outside this source record's bounded ordinary one-player slice.

The host fixture validates original script-table activation but does not prove full Android runtime wiring, frame-order behavior, rendered level completion, or the separate GhostAmbushHallway template path.
Arbitrary ScriptManager commands, skip/cutscene policy, full task/level save serialization, online/multi-player producers and full original manager body reconstruction are outside this adapter.
Generic diagnostic scheduler unsupported-command no-ops are not allowed for the selected live Crypt program; SpawnSession accepts only Wait and SpawnCharacter.

Original ObjectManager lookup filters by module ID (unless global/special-player policy applies). Current uniquely named pair is bounded; repeated-module expansion requires that producer and ownership model, not a global-name assumption.
Native integration source presence and host tests do not themselves prove Android runtime/rendered gameplay success. Device evidence must be reported separately with the tested APK identity.
Fresh Ghost Spawn/Idle/body services are bounded. Autonomous combat/AI, broad revival, weighted Hallway actors and full campaign reconstruction remain separate work.
Original Wait uses signed int elapsed addition. The bounded scheduler uses saturated uint32 elapsed arithmetic for exposed extreme dt; ordinary application frame dt is the reconstructed path.
CharacterGroup construction, membership add/remove and lifetime ownership are not reconstructed here.
GroupInfo::OnDied, OnEnemySpotted, broader status producers, and CharAI linked-aggro death/revival cleanup remain separate source work.
Character::CanRespawn's outer respawnability and delay checks are caller facts and are not implemented by this kernel.
Native coordinator/SpawnFacts wiring is not part of this host-only source slice.
CharAI outgoing/incoming tree storage and source map traversal are not owned by this kernel.

Native map storage, actor-identity mapping, selected AI notification consumer, and the exact effects inside OnDeAggro are adapter responsibilities; no linked actor graph or renderer integration is claimed.
Actor-owned AI/Lua consumers are not bound by this kernel. CharAI::OnDeAggro forwards to CharAIScript when present; no direct Lua callback is claimed here.
Implementing strong retained ownership is a caller responsibility; the kernel guarantees all-holds-before-mutation, held-handle lookup/erase/dispatch, and release-after-the-snapshot.
CharAI::AI_ClearAllAggroTowardMe(bool), including its termination path and optional current-target cleanup, is separate and not implemented.
CharacterGroup construction, membership registration/removal, aggro acquisition, automatic target selection, combat, and revive presentation remain separate.
The live Character property sheet, property recalculation pipeline and source object layout are caller-owned; this adapter accepts a raw resolved value through a callback.
GroupInfo construction, membership storage, member lifetime, OnDied/OnEnemySpotted status producers, and native group ownership are not implemented.
CSLimbus::OnFocus timer eligibility and PlayerManager local-host policy, timer event 0x2f delivery, and native Character coordinator wiring are deliberately deferred.
The source byte at Character+0x1481 is not semantically renamed beyond the observed InitSpawned suppression behavior.

The host kernel is not wired into the current Android actor/state native path; integration must supply live Character+0x520/+0x530/+0x1481, resolved property 11, PlayerManager policy and AI cleanup services.
PlayerManager::IsLocalPlayerHosting internals and native PlayerManager/OnlineGameState ownership remain outside the adapter.
The existing Character Coordinator owns the native timer slots, but event 0x2f delivery back into the game's revive/respawn state and source UI/effects are not proven by this kernel.
Original callbacks do not return adapter failure codes. Port-only callback failures preserve completed prior effects, do not roll back, and do not invoke the normal-path AI cleanup artificially.
Earlier OnBlur controller/visibility/pose/Revive operations remain separate and are not repeated by this producer.
Member registration, GroupInfo creation and ownership, network/checkpoint actors, and Native renderer binding remain outside this module.
Service errors are port protocol; completed callback effects are not rolled back.
No owner/player enemy gate is added to this TargetList query.
The existing character_target_search kernel is for the separate melee flags-1/filter-0 caller and is not invoked or modified.

Search service failures, pointer validation, bounded heap capacity, and opaque Character/room lifetimes are adapter boundaries. A source service error can occur after earlier candidates have been processed; no rollback is claimed.

The `_UpdateAggro` shared turn/delay/random prefix, highest-aggro branch, friend/neutral/enemy classifier, aggro storage mutation, Character event gates, script callback, and controller pursuit are separate and not implemented here.
Original tie behavior is only covered by the strict source comparator and copied priority-queue heap mechanics; the source does not guarantee a stable identity order for equal distances.
Full AISExternal lifecycle, InitVCB/OnInit dynamic level, entity methods/metatables, other callbacks, combat, buffs and timers remain outside this session.
CharAI owner/group enemy gate, source event9 candidate production, actor/controller/path source implementations and Native ownership are not wired here.
Single owning thread and externally retained services/actors are required; destroying the session from its own callback is unsupported.
Allocation cap is reused from source VM; no instruction cap or untrusted-script sandbox is added.

Production must not link both Adam and separate lua-runtime raw Lua cores with duplicate lua_* symbols and differing integer configurations; one compatible shared core or explicit engine isolation is required.
